newsitem.title: USA: Calif. floods could cost state $700 mln -officials.
newsitem.headline: Calif. floods could cost state $700 mln -officials.

text.p: Recent flooding in California could cost state government and its agencies more than $700 million, state officials estimated on Wednesday.
Of the total, the state's general fund could be responsible for up to $150 million. The local government share was estimated at $20 million.
The balance of over $500 million should be reimbursed by the federal government, officials with the state's Department of Finance estimated.

"Because we are still in a recovery effort and because state agencies are getting more information, these numbers will be revised and may move around," said H.D. Palmer, assistant director of the department.
The $700 million estimate included state costs for public assistance, road work and other recovery-related expenses resulting from the January storms.
The department of finance estimate did not include private losses incurred by individuals or businesses in the state, Palmer said.

A total of 46 of California's 58 counties are now under state of emergency declarations, state officials said. Nearly 16,000 homes have been damaged or destroyed in the flooding, according to state figures.
